task: For this synthetic writing exercise, use the fictional reporting notes to write a straight news story for a general newspaper audience. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 15, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Meridian Heights City Council voted 6 to 3 Tuesday night to approve a rezoning plan for a 28-acre former rail yard in the city's northeast corridor.
The vote occurred at the Tuesday, April 15, 2025, regular council session.
The rail yard, known as the Northline Site, was closed by Meridian Central Railroad in 2019.
The rezoning allows mixed-use residential and commercial development up to 14 stories.
The plan, proposed by Anchor Point Development Corp., calls for approximately 1,200 units of housing.
Under the city's inclusionary housing ordinance, at least 20 percent of units — approximately 240 — must be priced as affordable to households earning 80 percent or less of area median income.
Council President Diane Vasquez voted in favor and said: "This is a decade of negotiation finally bearing fruit."
Dissenting council member Marcus Okafor said: "We are approving density without a clear answer on whether the pipes can handle it."
The three no votes were cast by Okafor, Rhonda Tran, and Eli Suárez, all citing infrastructure readiness concerns.

City planning director Rebecca Lim told the council that a water main capacity study completed in January 2025 found the corridor would require $14 million in infrastructure upgrades to support the planned density.
The $14 million infrastructure cost is not included in the rezoning approval and must be addressed in a separate capital budget process.
A representative of Anchor Point said the company would fund the water infrastructure upgrades if the city agreed to a 10-year tax abatement on the project.
The council voted separately to table the tax abatement discussion until the June budget cycle.
The Meridian Residents Coalition submitted a petition opposing the plan signed by 2,300 residents.
Anchor Point must submit a final site plan within 18 months of the rezoning approval.
If built as proposed, the development would add an estimated 2,000 to 2,400 residents to a corridor currently served by one bus line.
The council meeting ran nearly four hours and included 47 public speakers; 31 spoke in favor and 16 opposed.
A prior rezoning attempt for the Northline Site failed in 2021 on a 4-to-5 vote.
Vasquez has represented the northeast district, which includes the Northline Site, since 2014.
Meridian Heights has a citywide housing shortage officially estimated at 8,500 units by the regional planning authority.

We are approving density without a clear answer on whether the pipes can handle it.
